source: Written 2026-10-22 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2026 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC26.K.ANR.1: Kindergarten: counting objects to 20 is written as lists of named things (no pictures); small groups seen at a glance are described by dot patterns, fingers and dice faces in words. One-to-one matching is tested through what a child says or touches, and through "one for each" situations.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.2: Kindergarten counting to 100: counting back is kept within 10 (starts at 10 or less); counting by tens starts at a multiple of 10. All answers are whole numbers up to 100.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.3: Written for Kindergarten: sets are numbers or short written lists, numbers to 20, no pictures. Differences use only counting back or up within 10.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.4: Every number and every answer is within 10, and objects and drawings are written out in words (no pictures). Unknown-start and unknown-change stories are left out as Grade 1 content; 'how many more to make 10' is kept because the summary names making 10.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.5: Targets the summary: add and subtract 0 or 1 within 10, and facts within 5. Kindergarten level, one step only; number-sentence choice questions use true/false sentences. Missing-number questions are limited to start-and-result facts within 5.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.6: Teen numbers 11-19 as ten and some more, composing and decomposing. No comparison problems (pass A flagged the two-step "how many more" compare as Grade 1). Place-value digit questions left out as Grade 1; counting is limited to counting on from 10 in ones.
notes.NC26.K.ANR.7: Kindergarten: text only, no repeated-addition counts beyond what can be counted one by one; all totals within 10.
notes.NC26.K.RD.1: Kindergarten: objects are written out as short lists (up to 20). No question asks how much more or less. 69 questions written.
notes.NC26.K.RD.2: Kindergarten: graphs are written out as lists of counts (all within 10, totals within 10). No question asks how much more or fewer in a comparison, only which is more or fewer. 69 questions written.
notes.NC26.K.SGMR.1: Kindergarten: text only; sums kept within 10 (one flagged-free exception none); solid shapes described by flat faces and everyday objects, not by corners or edges.
notes.NC26.K.SGMR.2: Drawing and building cannot be done on a screen, so the questions ask what a child would draw, build or put together (how many sides, sticks or corners, which shape, what a combination makes). Squares and rectangles are never offered together as options where both could fit; a 'rectangle' is described by 2 long and 2 short sides. Not testable in text: actually drawing or building.
notes.NC26.K.SGMR.3: No pictures: objects are compared by familiar real things with a clear order, by units counted out in words (cubes, blocks, beads, clips), or by short statements. No 'how much longer' or added-difference questions (Grade 1), and no chained comparisons (A taller than B, B taller than C), which pass A's solver flagged. Not testable in text: lining objects up side by side, or feeling weight in the hand.

questions.stem: We count: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. What number comes next?
questions.solution: Each number we say is one more than the number before it. After 7 comes 8.

solve.work: Counting 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; the number after 7 is 8.

questions.stem: Mia counts out loud: 8, 9, 10, 11. Which number does she say next?
questions.solution: After 11 comes 12. The number 11 was already said, 10 comes before it, and 13 skips a number.

solve.work: 8, 9, 10, 11; the number after 11 is 12. Only the option 12 fits.

questions.stem: Tom has these toys: car, ball, bear, doll, kite. How many toys does Tom have?
questions.solution: Count each toy one time: car 1, ball 2, bear 3, doll 4, kite 5. Tom has 5 toys.

solve.work: car (1), ball (2), bear (3), doll (4), kite (5). Five toys.

questions.stem: Sam lines up his cars in a row: red, blue, red, blue, red, blue, red. How many cars are in the row?

solve.work: red, blue, red, blue, red, blue, red: 7 cars (4 red, 3 blue). Distractors 3 and 4 are the colour counts.

solve.work: 6, 3, 8, 5: least is 3.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Three bags have 4, 7 and 5 candies. How many candies are in the bag that has the most?
questions.solution: 7 is more than 4 and more than 5, so the most is 7.

solve.work: 4, 7, 5: most is 7.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Ann has 2 pens. Bea has 5 pens. Cy has 3 pens. Who has the most pens?
choices: Ann and Cy have the most
questions.solution: 5 is more than 2 and more than 3, so Bea has the most pens.

solve.work: Ann 2, Bea 5, Cy 3: Bea has the most.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Write the smallest number: 8, 4 or 6.
questions.solution: 4 comes before 6 and 8 when you count, so 4 is the smallest.

solve.work: 8, 4, 6: smallest is 4.

questions.stem: Ella has 6 grapes. Fay has 1 more grape than Ella. How many grapes does Fay have?
questions.solution: 1 more than 6 is 7.

questions.stem: Which number is more than 7?
questions.solution: 9 comes after 7 when you count, so 9 is more than 7.

questions.stem: Write the number that is 1 more than 8.
questions.solution: Counting up from 8, the next number is 9.

solve.work: 1 more than 8 is 9.

questions.stem: Lily has 3 pennies. Kit wants more pennies than Lily. How many pennies could Kit have?
questions.solution: Kit needs more than 3. Only 5 is more than 3.

solve.work: More than 3: of 1, 2, 5, 3 only 5.

questions.stem: Hal has 7 stickers. Ida has 1 fewer sticker than Hal. How many stickers does Ida have?
questions.solution: 1 fewer than 7 is 6.

questions.stem: Dan has 6 hats and 6 coats. He matches each hat with one coat. How many coats have no hat?
questions.solution: There are 6 hats and 6 coats, so each hat gets its own coat and each coat gets its own hat. The sets are equal, so 0 coats are left with no hat.

solve.work: 6 hats match 6 coats one to one, so no coat is left without a hat: 0.

questions.stem: Ana has 7 grapes. Ben has 1 fewer grape than Ana. How many grapes does Ben have?
questions.solution: Ben has one fewer than 7 grapes. Counting back one from 7 gives 6. Ben has 6 grapes.

solve.work: 1 fewer than 7 is 6.

questions.stem: Kim has 9 stickers. Which friend has fewer stickers than Kim?
questions.solution: Fewer than 9 means a smaller number of stickers. 5 is less than 9. 12 and 10 are more, and 9 is the same.

solve.work: Fewer than 9: only 5 (Sam). 9 is equal; 10 and 12 are more.

questions.stem: Ava's pile has 15 shells. Ben's pile has 12 shells. How many shells are in the pile that has more shells?
questions.solution: 15 is more than 12, so Ava has more. Her pile has 15 shells.

solve.work: 15 vs 12: 15 is more, so the larger pile has 15 shells.

questions.stem: Which sentence about numbers is true?
questions.solution: Count up: 14, 15, 16, 17. 17 comes after 14, so 17 is more than 14.

solve.work: 17 comes after 14, so 17 is more than 14. Only that sentence is true.

questions.stem: Set A: cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube. Set B: cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube, cube. Which is true?
choices: Set A has more than Set B
Set B has more than Set A
Set A and Set B are the same
Set A has fewer than Set B
questions.answer: Set A and Set B are the same
questions.solution: Each set has 10 cubes. 10 and 10 are the same number.

solve.answer: Set A and Set B are the same
solve.work: Counted: Set A has 10 cubes, Set B has 10 cubes. Equal, so they are the same.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Look at these numbers: 16, 11, 20, 13. Write the least number.
questions.solution: Count up: 11, 13, 16, 20. 11 comes first, so 11 is the least.

solve.work: 16, 11, 20, 13: the smallest is 11.

questions.stem: Ravi has 12 buttons. Mia wants more buttons than Ravi. Which number of buttons could Mia have?
questions.solution: Mia needs more than 12. 15 is more than 12. 10 and 9 are less, and 12 is the same.

solve.work: More than 12: of 15, 12, 10, 9 only 15.

questions.stem: Write the number that is 1 fewer than 15.
questions.solution: 1 fewer than 15 is the number just before 15 when we count. That is 14.

solve.work: 1 fewer than 15 is the number just before it, 14.

questions.stem: Which two numbers are the same?
questions.solution: Same numbers are equal. Only 12 and 12 are the same.

solve.work: Only 12 and 12 are equal; the other pairs differ.

questions.stem: Set A: heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart. Set B: heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart, heart. How many hearts are in the set that has fewer hearts?
questions.solution: Set A has 12 hearts. Set B has 9 hearts. 9 is fewer than 12, so the answer is 9.

solve.work: Counted: Set A has 12 hearts, Set B has 9 hearts. 9 is fewer, so the answer is 9.

questions.stem: Eli has 10 cards. Pia has 8 cards. Eli says they have the same number of cards. Is Eli right?
choices: Yes. They have the same number.
questions.solution: 10 is more than 8, so the numbers are not the same. Eli has more cards than Pia.

solve.work: Eli 10, Pia 8: not the same. 10 is more than 8, so Eli has more. 'No. Eli has more cards.'

questions.stem: A bag has 14 red blocks. Dee wants the same number of blue blocks in another bag. How many blue blocks does Dee need?
questions.solution: Same number means equal. Dee needs 14 blue blocks.

solve.work: Same number as 14 red blocks: 14 blue blocks.

questions.stem: Set A has 14 dots and Set B has 17 dots. How many dots are in the set that has more?
questions.solution: 17 is more than 14, so the set with more has 17 dots.

questions.stem: A shelf has 13 books. A box has 16 books. Which is true?
choices: The shelf has more books than the box
The shelf and the box have the same number of books
The box has more books than the shelf
The box has fewer books than the shelf
questions.answer: The box has more books than the shelf
questions.solution: 16 is more than 13, so the box has more books.

solve.answer: The box has more books than the shelf
solve.work: Shelf 13, box 16. 16 > 13, so the box has more.

questions.stem: Zoe counts 18 ants on a log and 11 ants on a rock. How many ants are in the group that has fewer?
questions.solution: 11 is less than 18, so the group with fewer has 11 ants.

questions.stem: Mei has 12 stickers on her book and 15 stickers on her desk. She says the desk has fewer stickers. Is she right?
choices: Yes. The desk has fewer stickers.
No. The book has more stickers.
No. They have the same number of stickers.
No. The desk has more stickers.
questions.answer: No. The desk has more stickers.
questions.solution: 15 is more than 12, so the desk has more stickers. Mei is not right.

solve.answer: No. The desk has more stickers.
solve.work: Book 12, desk 15. 15 > 12, so the desk has more; Mei is wrong. "The book has more" is false.

questions.stem: Which number is greater than 12?
questions.solution: Only 15 comes after 12 when you count.

questions.stem: Write the number that is less than 14 and more than 12.
questions.solution: Counting up: 12, 13, 14. The number between 12 and 14 is 13.

solve.work: Between 12 and 14: 13.

questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: 16 comes before 19 when you count, so 16 is less than 19.

solve.work: 16 < 19, so "16 is less than 19".

questions.stem: Of the numbers 13 and 16, write the one that is less.
questions.solution: 13 comes before 16 when you count, so 13 is less.

questions.stem: A class has 15 chairs and the same number of desks. How many desks are there?
questions.solution: The same number as 15 is 15.

solve.work: Same number as 15 chairs: 15 desks.

questions.stem: Ivy has 17 beads. Jay has 17 beads. Kai has 16 beads. Which two children have the same number of beads?
questions.solution: Ivy and Jay both have 17. Kai has 16, which is different.

solve.work: Ivy 17, Jay 17, Kai 16. Ivy and Jay match.

questions.stem: Two boxes hold the same number of crayons. One box holds 16 crayons. How many crayons does the other box hold?
questions.solution: The same number as 16 is 16.

solve.work: Same number: 16.

questions.stem: Two bags have the same number of marbles. One bag has 18 marbles. Which could be the number in the other bag?
questions.solution: The other bag has the same number, 18.

solve.work: Same number as 18: must be 18.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Four boxes have 12, 9, 15 and 10 crayons. How many crayons are in the box that has the fewest?
questions.solution: 9 is less than 10, 12 and 15, so the fewest is 9.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Pam has 13 stickers. Quin has 17 stickers. Rick has 14 stickers. Sue has 11 stickers. Who has the most stickers?
questions.solution: 17 is the greatest of 13, 17, 14 and 11, so Quin has the most.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Write the greatest number: 11, 18, 13 or 16.
questions.solution: 18 comes after 11, 13 and 16 when you count, so 18 is the greatest.

questions.stem: Write the number that is 1 more than 14.
questions.solution: Counting up from 14, the next number is 15.

solve.work: 1 more than 14 is 15.

questions.stem: Pete has 16 leaves. Which number of leaves is more than Pete has?
questions.solution: Only 19 comes after 16 when you count.

solve.work: More than 16: of 19, 14, 16, 12 only 19.

questions.stem: A tray has 13 muffins. Another tray has 1 more muffin than that tray. How many muffins are on the other tray?
questions.solution: 1 more than 13 is 14.

questions.stem: Hugo has 10 cards. Which change gives Hugo more cards?
questions.solution: Getting 2 more cards makes the number of cards go up. The other changes keep it the same or make it less.

solve.work: Getting 2 more gives 12 > 10; the others give 8, 10, 9.

questions.stem: Wren has 13 cookies. Which number of cookies is fewer than 13?
questions.solution: 11 comes before 13 when you count, so it is fewer.

solve.work: Fewer than 13: of 11, 13, 16, 14 only 11.

questions.stem: Rick has 17 marbles. He wants to have fewer marbles. Which change does that?
questions.solution: Giving marbles away makes the number go down. The other changes make it go up or keep it the same.

solve.work: Giving 2 away gives 15 < 17; the others give 17, 19, 18.

questions.stem: A shelf has 18 books. A second shelf has 1 fewer book than the first shelf. How many books are on the second shelf?
questions.solution: 1 fewer than 18 is 17.

questions.stem: A shelf holds 20 books. A second shelf holds 1 fewer book than the first shelf. How many books are on the second shelf?
questions.solution: One fewer than 20 is the number we say just before 20 when we count up. That number is 19.

solve.work: 1 fewer than 20 is 19.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Tom has 12 coins. Uma has 9 coins. Val has 15 coins. Wes has 11 coins. Who has the fewest coins?
questions.solution: Count up: 9, 11, 12, 15. 9 is the least, and Uma has 9 coins.

solve.work: Tom 12, Uma 9, Val 15, Wes 11. Fewest is 9: Uma.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Pia has 17 beads. Quinn has 18 beads. Ross has 16 beads. How many beads does the child with the most beads have?
questions.solution: Count up: 16, 17, 18. 18 is the most, so the answer is 18.

solve.work: 17, 18, 16: most is 18 (Quinn).

questions.stem: Which number is more than 17 and less than 20?
questions.solution: Count: 17, 18, 19, 20. 18 comes after 17 and before 20. 16 and 17 are not more than 17, and 20 is not less than 20.

solve.work: More than 17 and less than 20 means 18 or 19. Of the options (17, 20, 16, 18) only 18 fits.

questions.stem: Hal has 15 cards. Ivy has 13 cards. Which change gives Ivy more cards than Hal?
questions.solution: Ivy needs more than 15. 13 and 3 more is 16, and 16 is more than 15. With 1 more she has 14 (fewer), with 2 more she has 15 (the same), and putting 2 away leaves 11.

solve.work: Hal 15, Ivy 13. +3 gives 16 > 15 (more). +2 gives 15 (same). +1 gives 14 (fewer). Putting 2 away gives 11 (fewer). Only 'gets 3 more'.

questions.stem: Ola has fewer shells than Ned. Ned has 11 shells. Which could be the number of shells Ola has?
questions.solution: Ola has fewer than 11. 8 is fewer than 11. 14 and 12 are more than 11, and 11 is the same.

solve.work: Fewer than 11: of 8, 12, 11, 14 only 8.

questions.stem: Jo has 17 coins. Kit has the same number of coins as Jo. Lee has 1 more coin than Kit. How many coins does Lee have?
questions.solution: Kit has 17 coins, the same as Jo. Lee has 1 more than 17, which is 18.

solve.work: Kit = Jo = 17. Lee has 1 more than 17 = 18.

questions.stem: Mara has 18 stickers. Nico has 18 stickers. Mara gets 1 more sticker. Who has more stickers now?
choices: Mara and Nico have the same number
questions.solution: They both start with 18. Mara now has 19. 19 is more than 18, so Mara has more.

solve.work: Both 18; Mara gets 1 more so Mara 19, Nico 18. Mara has more than Nico.

questions.skill: Tell which sets are the same
questions.stem: Tom has 9 pennies. Pam has 9 pennies. Sue has 6 pennies. Which two children have the same number of pennies?
questions.solution: Tom has 9 and Pam has 9. Sue has 6, which is different. So Tom and Pam have the same number.

solve.work: Tom 9, Pam 9, Sue 6. Tom and Pam both have 9.

questions.stem: Pip has 16 marbles. Ann has 18 marbles. Bo has 16 marbles. Cy has 15 marbles. Di has 19 marbles. Which child has fewer marbles than Pip?
questions.solution: Pip has 16. Ann has 18 and Di has 19, which are more than 16. Bo has 16, which is the same. Cy has 15, which is fewer than 16.

solve.work: Pip has 16. Di 19 (more), Ann 18 (more), Cy 15 (fewer), Bo 16 (same). Only Cy has fewer.

questions.stem: Look at these numbers: 12, 19 and 15. Put them in order from the least to the greatest. Write the number in the middle.
questions.solution: The least is 12 and the greatest is 19. The number in the middle is 15.

solve.work: Order least to greatest: 12, 15, 19. Middle number is 15.

questions.stem: Box P has 17 cubes. Box Q has 18 cubes. Which is true?
choices: Box Q has more cubes than Box P
Box P has more cubes than Box Q
Box P and Box Q have the same number of cubes
Box Q has fewer cubes than Box P
questions.answer: Box Q has more cubes than Box P
questions.solution: 18 comes after 17, so 18 is more than 17. Box Q has more cubes.

solve.answer: Box Q has more cubes than Box P
solve.work: P 17, Q 18. 18 > 17, so Box Q has more.

questions.stem: Lena has 20 beads on one string and 19 beads on another string. How many beads are on the string that has fewer?
questions.solution: 19 comes just before 20, so 19 is less than 20. The string with fewer has 19 beads.

questions.stem: Jun has 15 buttons. Kim has 1 fewer button than Jun. Who has more buttons?
choices: Jun and Kim have the same number of buttons
questions.solution: Kim has 1 fewer than Jun, so Jun has more buttons.

solve.work: Kim has 15 - 1 = 14. 15 > 14, so Jun has more.

questions.stem: Pip has 20 stickers on a page and 16 stickers in a pocket. How many stickers are in the place that has fewer?
questions.solution: 16 is less than 20, so the place with fewer has 16 stickers.

questions.stem: Which number is more than 8 and less than 11?
questions.solution: 9 is the only choice that comes after 8 and before 11.

solve.work: More than 8 and less than 11: 9 or 10; only 9 is offered.

questions.stem: Count up from 14. What is the first number you say that is more than 16?
questions.solution: Counting up from 14: 14, 15, 16, 17. The first number more than 16 is 17.

solve.work: Counting 14, 15, 16, 17: first number more than 16 is 17.

questions.stem: Which pair shows a first number that is less than the second number?
questions.solution: 9 is less than 12. In the other pairs the first number is more than, or the same as, the second.

questions.stem: Write the greatest number that is less than 20.
questions.solution: 19 is just before 20 when you count, so it is the greatest number less than 20.

solve.work: Whole numbers less than 20: the greatest is 19.

questions.stem: Amy has 15 pennies. Ben has 15 pennies. Cal has 14 pennies. Who has the same number of pennies as Amy?
questions.solution: Amy and Ben both have 15. Cal has 14, which is different.

solve.work: Amy 15, Ben 15, Cal 14. Ben.

questions.stem: Jada has 9 stars. Ravi has 6 stars. Ravi gets more stars until he has the same number as Jada. How many stars does Ravi have then?
questions.solution: Ravi has the same number as Jada, which is 9.

solve.work: Ravi gets stars until he has as many as Jada: 9.

questions.stem: Which sentence tells about the same number of hats and coats?
questions.solution: Only 13 and 13 are the same number.

solve.work: Same number means equal: 13 hats and 13 coats.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Mo has 19 stickers. Ned has 17 stickers. Oz has 18 stickers. Pru has 20 stickers. Who has the fewest stickers?
questions.solution: 17 is less than 18, 19 and 20, so Ned has the fewest.

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Ana has 15 beads. Bo has 12 beads. Cy has 15 beads. Di has 9 beads. How many beads does the child with the fewest beads have?
questions.solution: 9 is less than 12 and less than 15, so the fewest is 9.

solve.work: 15, 12, 15, 9: fewest is 9 (Di).

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Gus has 17 coins. Hana has 19 coins. Ian has 19 coins. How many coins does the child with the most coins have?
questions.solution: 19 is more than 17. Hana and Ian both have 19, which is the most.

solve.work: 17, 19, 19: most is 19 (a tie, but the number is the same).

questions.skill: Find the most or the fewest of several
questions.stem: Which number is greater than all of these numbers: 12, 15 and 9?
questions.solution: 17 is more than 12, more than 15 and more than 9. The other choices are not more than 15.

solve.work: Must exceed 15: only 17.

questions.stem: Zed has 12 pebbles. He wants to have more than 14 pebbles. What is the fewest number of pebbles he can have then?
questions.solution: More than 14 starts at 15, so Zed needs at least 15 pebbles.

solve.issues: "fewest number of pebbles" is slightly awkward ("smallest number"); the two-step reading (he has 12, then wants more than 14) may confuse a K child, but one answer only.
solve.work: More than 14 means 15 or more; the fewest is 15. (The 12 he has now is background.)

questions.stem: Pia has 19 beads. Which number of beads is more than 19?
questions.solution: 20 comes right after 19, so 20 is more than 19.

solve.work: More than 19: of 10, 18, 20, 19 only 20.

questions.stem: Win has 9 apples. Xan has more apples than Win but fewer than 11. How many apples does Xan have?
questions.solution: The number more than 9 and fewer than 11 is 10.

solve.work: More than 9 and fewer than 11: 10.

questions.stem: Cy has 16 cards. Abe has 15 cards, Bea has 16 cards, Dot has 18 cards and Eli has 14 cards. Who has more cards than Cy?
questions.solution: 18 is more than 16. The others have 15, 16 or 14, which are not more than 16.

solve.work: Cy 16. Abe 15, Bea 16, Dot 18, Eli 14. Only Dot has more.

questions.stem: Bo has fewer than 12 cars. Which could be true?
questions.solution: Only 9 is fewer than 12.

solve.work: Fewer than 12: of 14, 9, 20, 12 only 9.

questions.stem: Cy has 14 cards. Cy wants fewer than 12 cards. What is the most cards Cy can have?
questions.solution: Fewer than 12 means 11 or less. The most is 11.

solve.work: Fewer than 12 means 11 or less; the most is 11.

questions.stem: Lia has 16 buttons. Mark has fewer buttons than Lia but more than 14. How many buttons does Mark have?
questions.solution: The number fewer than 16 and more than 14 is 15.

solve.work: Fewer than 16 and more than 14: 15.

questions.stem: Nell has 10 hats. Abe has 11 hats, Ben has 10 hats, Cal has 8 hats and Dan has 12 hats. Who has fewer hats than Nell?
questions.solution: 8 is fewer than 10. The others have 11, 10 or 12, which are not fewer than 10.

solve.work: Nell 10. Abe 11, Ben 10, Cal 8, Dan 12. Only Cal has fewer.

questions.stem: Sam has 4 blocks. He gets 3 more blocks. How many blocks does Sam have now?
questions.solution: Getting more means adding. 4 and 3 more is $4 + 3 = 7$.

solve.work: Joining: 4 blocks and 3 more. 4, then count on 5, 6, 7. 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.stem: What is $5 + 4$?
questions.solution: Start at 5 and count on 4: 6, 7, 8, 9. So $5 + 4 = 9$.

solve.work: 5 + 4: start at 5, count on 6, 7, 8, 9. Answer 9. Only option 9 matches.

questions.stem: There are 6 ducks in a pond. 2 ducks swim away. How many ducks are in the pond now?
questions.solution: Swimming away means taking away. $6 - 2 = 4$. There are 4 ducks left.

solve.work: Separating: 6 ducks, 2 swim away. 6 - 2 = 4. Option 4.

questions.stem: What is $8 - 3$?
questions.solution: Start at 8 and count back 3: 7, 6, 5. So $8 - 3 = 5$.

solve.work: 8 - 3: count back from 8: 7, 6, 5. Answer 5.

questions.skill: Putting together and taking apart (parts and whole)
questions.stem: A group has 2 girls and 5 boys. How many children are in the group?
questions.solution: Put the two parts together. $2 + 5 = 7$ children.

solve.work: Part-part-whole: 2 girls + 5 boys = 7 children.

questions.stem: Start at 5. Count on 2 more. Which number do you end on?
questions.solution: Count on from 5: 6, 7. You end on 7.

solve.work: Start at 5, count on 2: 6, 7. End on 7.

questions.skill: Writing and reading + and - number sentences
questions.stem: Ana has 3 apples. She gets 2 more apples. Which number sentence tells about this?
questions.solution: Ana starts with 3 and gets 2 more, so we add: $3 + 2 = 5$.

solve.work: 3 apples, gets 2 more: joining, 3 + 2 = 5. Other options: 3+3 (wrong addend), 3-2 (subtraction), 5+2 (wrong start).

questions.stem: $6 + ? = 10$. What number is the ?
questions.solution: Count on from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 4 steps. So the ? is 4.

solve.work: 6 + ? = 10. Count on from 6 to 10: 7, 8, 9, 10 is 4 counts. 6 + 4 = 10.

questions.stem: Which two numbers make 10 when you add them?
questions.solution: $7 + 3 = 10$. The others make 9, 11 and 8.

questions.skill: Adding and subtracting with objects and drawings
questions.stem: Tom draws 5 circles. He crosses out 2 of the circles. How many circles are not crossed out?
questions.solution: Crossing out means taking away. $5 - 2 = 3$ circles are not crossed out.

solve.work: 5 circles, 2 crossed out: 5 - 2 = 3 not crossed out.

questions.stem: There are 2 frogs on a log. 5 more frogs hop on. How many frogs are on the log now?
questions.solution: 2 and 5 more is $2 + 5 = 7$.

questions.stem: There are 5 cups. 1 cup is red. The rest are blue. How many cups are blue?
questions.solution: 5 is made of 1 and 4, so 4 cups are blue.

questions.stem: Jess counts: 6, 7, 8. What number does she say next?
questions.solution: After 8 comes 9.

questions.stem: Start at 8. Count back 2. Which number do you end on?
questions.solution: Counting back 2 from 8: 7, 6. You end on 6.

questions.stem: Pia is on step 2 of a staircase. She goes up 4 steps. What step is she on now?
questions.solution: Count on 4 from 2: 3, 4, 5, 6.

questions.solution: Joining 1 more to 4 is $4 + 1 = 5$.

questions.stem: Which number sentence has a minus sign?
questions.solution: The minus sign is the short line. Only $7 - 3 = 4$ has one.

solve.work: Only $7 - 3 = 4$ has a minus sign.

questions.stem: Nina has 9 pennies. How many more pennies does she need to have 10 pennies?
What number do you add to 5 to make 10?
Finish the ten: $10 = 2 + ?$ What number is the ?
Which sentence is true?
questions.solution: $1 + 9 = 10$. The others make 9, 11 and 9.

questions.stem: Max has 6 counters. He takes 2 counters away. How many counters are left?

questions.skill: Adding and subtracting with objects and drawings
questions.stem: Pip makes a row of 2 blocks and a row of 6 blocks. How many blocks are there in all?
Mia puts 6 red cubes in a tower. Then she puts 3 blue cubes on top. How many cubes are in the tower?
questions.solution: Join the red cubes and the blue cubes. $6 + 3 = 9$ cubes.

solve.work: 6 red cubes plus 3 blue cubes: 6 + 3 = 9 cubes in the tower.

questions.stem: A box has 9 pencils in it. Eli takes 4 pencils out of the box. How many pencils are left in the box?
questions.solution: Taking out means taking away. $9 - 4 = 5$ pencils are left.

solve.work: 9 pencils, 4 taken out: 9 - 4 = 5 left.

questions.stem: What is $10 - 6$?
questions.solution: Start at 10 and count back 6: 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4. So $10 - 6 = 4$.

questions.skill: Putting together and taking apart (parts and whole)
questions.stem: A bag has 7 marbles. Some are red and the rest are blue. Which could be true?
questions.solution: The red and the blue must make 7 in all. $3 + 4 = 7$. The others make 8, 6 and 8.

solve.work: Red + blue must total 7. 4+4=8, 3+4=7, 2+4=6, 3+5=8. Only 3 red and 4 blue works.

questions.skill: Putting together and taking apart (parts and whole)
questions.stem: There are 8 children at a table. 5 of them are boys. The rest are girls. How many girls are at the table?
questions.solution: The whole is 8. One part is 5. The other part is $8 - 5 = 3$ girls.

solve.work: Whole 8, part 5 boys, other part girls: 8 - 5 = 3.
